headline: Math is nearly saturated while real-world agent work remains the open frontier
outlook: Math has all but run out of road: models closed 95% of the remaining headroom there over the past year, and both FrontierMath and its Tier 4 set crossed 90% in recent months. Agents doing real work are the slowest-moving area, at 34% of headroom closed, with OSWorld 2 at 31.4% and the Remote Labor Index at 20.8%, even as APEX-Agents jumped from 68.6% to 82.2% in a single week of releases. The measure linking these is task length: the longest tasks models can handle now stand at 17.4 hours and have been doubling roughly every 4.1 months, which on current trends points to work-week-length tasks most likely around December, though the plausible range runs into August 2027. Meanwhile, GPQA-level capability has fallen from $3.44 to $0.055 per million tokens, so whatever agents can do next is likely to arrive cheaply. Treat the dates loosely, since past likely ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, and Terminal-Bench and GeoBench are both stalled behind their fitted trends.
